title: 2 Samuel 11: David, Bathsheba, and the Murder of Uriah
body:
Read the chapter → [2 Samuel 11](/bible/2-samuel/11)

## Introduction

Chapter 11 is the great fall. While the kings went forth to battle, David tarried at Jerusalem, saw Bathsheba washing herself, sent for her, and lay with her, and she conceived. David then schemed to cover it, calling Uriah home so it would appear the child was his; when the loyal Uriah refused to go down to his house, David sent him back to the front with a letter ordering his death. Bathsheba mourned, then David took her to wife, but the thing that David had done displeased the Most High. People who want to justify wrongdoing always run to David and Bathsheba, but David was a man just like the rest of us, and this was his mess up; it does not make the deed right, and we will see what the judgment was.

**[2 Samuel 11:1-5](/bible/2-samuel/11#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/2-samuel/11#v1)</sup> And it came to pass, after the year was expired, at the time when kings go forth to battle, that David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon, and besieged Rabbah. But David tarried still at Jerusalem.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/2-samuel/11#v2)</sup> And it came to pass in an eveningtide, that David arose from off his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king’s house: and from the roof he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/2-samuel/11#v3)</sup> And David sent and enquired after the woman. And one said, Is not this Bath–sheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/2-samuel/11#v4)</sup> And David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in unto him, and he lay with her; for she was purified from her uncleanness: and she returned unto her house.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/2-samuel/11#v5)</sup> And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I am with child.

- After the year was expired, at the time when kings go forth to battle, David sent Joab and all Israel to destroy the children of Ammon and besiege Rabbah, but David tarried still at Jerusalem. In the evening he walked upon the roof, saw a woman washing herself who was very beautiful, inquired and learned she was Bathsheba the wife of Uriah the Hittite, sent and took her, and lay with her; and she conceived and told David, I am with child.
- Masons and people in these fraternities always run here to justify wrongdoing, saying David slept with Bathsheba and the Most High still forgave him. But you are not King David; David was a man like the rest of us, and he messed up, and this is the mess up. About ninety percent of them go right back to David and Bathsheba every time they want to justify some wrongdoing.

**[2 Samuel 11:6-10](/bible/2-samuel/11#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/2-samuel/11#v6)</sup> And David sent to Joab, saying, Send me Uriah the Hittite. And Joab sent Uriah to David.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/2-samuel/11#v7)</sup> And when Uriah was come unto him, David demanded of him how Joab did, and how the people did, and how the war prospered.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/2-samuel/11#v8)</sup> And David said to Uriah, Go down to thy house, and wash thy feet. And Uriah departed out of the king’s house, and there followed him a mess of meat from the king.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/2-samuel/11#v9)</sup> But Uriah slept at the door of the king’s house with all the servants of his lord, and went not down to his house.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/2-samuel/11#v10)</sup> And when they had told David, saying, Uriah went not down unto his house, David said unto Uriah, Camest thou not from thy journey? why then didst thou not go down unto thine house?

- David sent to Joab to send him Uriah. When Uriah came, David asked how Joab and the people did and how the war prospered, then told him to go down to his house and wash his feet, sending a mess of meat after him. But Uriah slept at the door of the king's house with the servants of his lord and went not down to his house. When David heard it, he asked Uriah why he came not from his journey and went not down.
- David's plan, which nobody was privy to, was that if Uriah went down and slept with his wife, they could say the child was his. A lot of us do that today: many people raise children that are not theirs, and just because David did it does not make it right.

**[2 Samuel 11:11-13](/bible/2-samuel/11#v11)**

> <sup>[11](/bible/2-samuel/11#v11)</sup> And Uriah said unto David, The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in tents; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, are encamped in the open fields; shall I then go into mine house, to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? as thou livest, and as thy soul liveth, I will not do this thing.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/2-samuel/11#v12)</sup> And David said to Uriah, Tarry here to day also, and to morrow I will let thee depart. So Uriah abode in Jerusalem that day, and the morrow.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/2-samuel/11#v13)</sup> And when David had called him, he did eat and drink before him; and he made him drunk: and at even he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but went not down to his house.

- Uriah told David that the ark and Israel and Judah abode in tents, and Joab and the servants of his lord were encamped in the open fields; so how could he go into his house to eat, drink, and lie with his wife? As David lived, he would not do this thing. David kept him another day and made him drunk, but that evening Uriah still went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord and went not down to his house.
- Uriah had a sense of loyalty that was probably killing David all the more, because David could not deceive this man into laying with his wife. Even drunk, when a man might just go home to sleep it off, Uriah still slept at David's house and would not go down.

**[2 Samuel 11:14-17](/bible/2-samuel/11#v14)**

> <sup>[14](/bible/2-samuel/11#v14)</sup> And it came to pass in the morning, that David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/2-samuel/11#v15)</sup> And he wrote in the letter, saying, Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/2-samuel/11#v16)</sup> And it came to pass, when Joab observed the city, that he assigned Uriah unto a place where he knew that valiant men were.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/2-samuel/11#v17)</sup> And the men of the city went out, and fought with Joab: and there fell some of the people of the servants of David; and Uriah the Hittite died also.

- In the morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah, ordering that Uriah be set in the forefront of the hottest battle and then abandoned, that he might be smitten and die. Joab assigned Uriah to a place where he knew valiant men were, and when the men of the city fought, some of David's servants fell, and Uriah the Hittite died also.
- David set this man up to get murdered, and Israel does this too, contrary to popular belief. This goes back to Deuteronomy 27: cursed is he that smiteth his neighbour secretly, because nobody knew what David was doing, and cursed is he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. The reward was that woman; he slew an innocent man who had done nothing.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 27:24-25](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v24)**
    > <sup>[24](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v24)</sup> Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly. And all the people shall say, Amen.
    >
    > <sup>[25](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v25)</sup> Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. And all the people shall say, Amen.

    Cursed is he that smiteth his neighbour secretly, and cursed is he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person.

**[2 Samuel 11:18-25](/bible/2-samuel/11#v18)**

> <sup>[18](/bible/2-samuel/11#v18)</sup> Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war;
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/2-samuel/11#v19)</sup> And charged the messenger, saying, When thou hast made an end of telling the matters of the war unto the king,
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/2-samuel/11#v20)</sup> And if so be that the king’s wrath arise, and he say unto thee, Wherefore approached ye so nigh unto the city when ye did fight? knew ye not that they would shoot from the wall?
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/2-samuel/11#v21)</sup> Who smote Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? did not a woman cast a piece of a millstone upon him from the wall, that he died in Thebez? why went ye nigh the wall? then say thou, Thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/2-samuel/11#v22)</sup> So the messenger went, and came and shewed David all that Joab had sent him for.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/2-samuel/11#v23)</sup> And the messenger said unto David, Surely the men prevailed against us, and came out unto us into the field, and we were upon them even unto the entering of the gate.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/2-samuel/11#v24)</sup> And the shooters shot from off the wall upon thy servants; and some of the king’s servants be dead, and thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/2-samuel/11#v25)</sup> Then David said unto the messenger, Thus shalt thou say unto Joab, Let not this thing displease thee, for the sword devoureth one as well as another: make thy battle more strong against the city, and overthrow it: and encourage thou him.

- Joab sent and told David all concerning the war, charging the messenger that if the king's wrath arose over drawing so nigh the city, he should then say that Uriah the Hittite was dead also. When the messenger delivered it, David told him to say to Joab, Let not this thing displease thee, for the sword devoureth one as well as another; make the battle stronger and overthrow the city.
- Other men of Israel died too, not just Uriah, so with David's sin other men died as well. Joab knew what the king really wanted, so he made sure to name Uriah as dead. David's reply was that it is what it is, the mission was accomplished, you win some and lose some; being content with murder is a wicked thing to do.

**[2 Samuel 11:26-27](/bible/2-samuel/11#v26)**

> <sup>[26](/bible/2-samuel/11#v26)</sup> And when the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she mourned for her husband.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/2-samuel/11#v27)</sup> And when the mourning was past, David sent and fetched her to his house, and she became his wife, and bare him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased the Lord.

- When the wife of Uriah heard her husband was dead, she mourned for him, and when the mourning was past, David sent and fetched her to his house and she became his wife and bare him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased the Most High.
- It displeased the Most High because it was murder; he set the man up to be murdered on a battlefield, which was not a righteous thing. Bathsheba was not innocent either; she was complicit. When David called for her she went, she did not refuse because she was married, and it was consensual, not rape. She knew she was pregnant, so this was deceitful on both sides.
